nodes.title: Derive the parent checkbox from the children
nodes.why: The parent has no state of its own: allChecked feeds its [checked] binding, so the box matches the children after every change.
nodes.alternative: Keep a separate parentChecked flag, or set checked and indeterminate on the element through a ViewChild after every change.
nodes.tradeoff: Bindings replace direct DOM writes, but the parent is only as correct as the children array it is computed from.

nodes.title: Derive the mixed parent state
nodes.why: Partial selection is a state of its own: bound to the native indeterminate property, it shows the mixed mark while checked stays false.
nodes.alternative: Treat any selected child as a fully checked parent.
nodes.tradeoff: The parent now has three visual states, which accurately communicates the child aggregate.

nodes.title: Apply parent selection to every child
nodes.why: Copying every child with the parent's new value gives the signal a new array, so the child bindings and both computed flags update together for select-all and clear-all.
nodes.alternative: Loop over the children and assign child.checked in place.
nodes.tradeoff: The map allocates three small objects per click, while in-place writes would keep the old array and leave the computed flags on their cached values.

nodes.title: Toggle one child by replacing it
nodes.why: Only the clicked child becomes a new object; the new array lets checkedCount, allChecked and someChecked recompute while the other rows keep their objects.
nodes.alternative: Bind each child with [(ngModel)]="child.checked", which writes into the object inside the signal's array.
nodes.tradeoff: Each child input needs [checked] plus a (change) handler instead of one two-way binding, but every change goes through the signal.
